reviewMethod: Model-assisted editorial review with exact-delta preservation and deterministic regression checks.

before.exampleAnswer: More ordered pairs make 7 than make 2

after.exampleAnswer: Six equally likely ordered pairs total 7, whereas only (1, 1) totals 2. Probabilities depend on the number of matching pairs, not just the list of possible sums.

before.exampleAnswer: Whenever the outcomes are equally likely

after.exampleAnswer: The favourable-count divided by total-count shortcut requires equally likely outcomes. If their probabilities differ, add the probabilities of the favourable outcomes instead.

before.exampleAnswer: Only outcomes compatible with the clue

after.exampleAnswer: Conditioning restricts the sample space to outcomes compatible with the clue. Count favourable outcomes within that same restricted set.

before.exampleAnswer: Knowing one event does not change the probability of the other

after.exampleAnswer: Events are independent when learning that one occurred does not change the other's probability, when the conditional probability is defined. Equivalently, their joint probability is the product.
The events are mutually exclusive: one roll cannot be both 1 and 2. They are not independent, because knowing that 1 occurred makes the probability of 2 zero.

before.exampleAnswer: The mean rises and the median stays 4

after.exampleAnswer: Replacing 5 with 25 increases the total and hence the mean. The sorted middle observation is still 4, so the median is unchanged.

before.exampleAnswer: For an even count it averages the two sorted middle values

after.exampleAnswer: Sort the data before locating its centre. With an even count, the median is the average of the two middle observations and need not itself be observed.
Both datasets average 4. The first has no deviation from that mean, while the second has observations two units below or above it.

before.exampleAnswer: A whole-population variance divides by its count; the usual unbiased sample estimate divides by one less

after.exampleAnswer: For the full population, average squared deviations by dividing by N. The usual unbiased sample estimate of population variance divides by n − 1 because the mean was estimated from the sample.

before.exampleAnswer: It shows agreement here, without guaranteeing agreement elsewhere

after.exampleAnswer: Agreement in this constructed sample is evidence about this case only. It does not guarantee that another sample or another measured quantity will agree.

before.exampleAnswer: Other parts of the target population are systematically excluded

after.exampleAnswer: The sampling frame omits people who do not visit that gym on weekdays. Increasing responses within that frame does not remove the systematic exclusion.

before.exampleAnswer: Selection by chance with known, nonzero inclusion probabilities

after.exampleAnswer: A probability sample uses chance selection with known, nonzero inclusion probabilities. Those probabilities can differ between units; equal probabilities are a special case.
